conviction_note: Event confirmed by the company's own 2026-09-17 release; the only documentary edge is that SBA debentures were fully drawn (+$46m) and the Valley SPV facility +$15m between May 31 and Sep 21, which shows deployment and partly offsets a Q2 NII bar ($0.49, one confirmed source) sitting above the $0.47 run-rate on a name whose consensus was missed by $0.07 in each of the last two prints; the forward 6%->8% refinancing cost roughly cancels the Sept 16 Fed hike benefit, so the net is a small negative on a stock already at its 52-week low, 0.72x May NAV and pricing a dividend cut.
bar: Adjusted NII $0.49/share, total investment income $31.47m, MarketBeat preview dated 2026-09-29 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-saratoga-investment-sar-set-to-announce-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-09-29/). A second agreeing source could not be retrieved; Benzinga's page carried a stale $0.54. The company gives no NII guidance. So the bar is single-source and every size on the name is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest is low but the sources disagree: one aggregator shows ~593k shares, 3.65% of float, 6.69 days to cover, and Fintel shows ~198k shares, 1.49% of float, 1.9 days (both from a search snippet, late Sept 2026; fintel.io and the Nasdaq short-interest API returned 403/503 when fetched directly). Not a crowded short. There is no usable option chain (total open interest 0), so there is no skew. The tape lean is negative: -9.2% over 20 days, -4.6% over 5 days, at the 52-week low, -32% from the high. The ex-dividend date ($0.25 monthly, record 2026-10-06) is the event day itself, so it falls before the close-to-close window starts.

findings.finding: The Q2 bar of $0.49 implies about +4% QoQ against Q1's $0.47 adjusted NII, which itself carried elevated structuring fees ($0.66m vs $0.26m a year earlier). Interest expense rose with SBA and Valley draws, a full quarter of the April 7.25% notes and 5 days of double carry on the 8% 2031 notes. Consensus was missed by $0.07 at each of the last two prints ($0.58 vs $0.65 and $0.47 vs $0.54). The print is more likely at or slightly under the bar than above it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NII misses with NAV declines were sold: Q1 FY27 (0.47 vs 0.54, NAV -4.9%) -14.09%; Q2 FY26 (0.58 vs 0.65) -4.71%; Q4 FY26 (0.53 with excise) -3.10%. The one NII and NAV uptick (Q3 FY26) bought +1.55%.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar was set by six analysts who have over-forecast this name twice in a row. If the market already expected a sub-bar print, the consensus would have come down to ~$0.47 rather than sitting $0.02 above run-rate. It is only partly priced: at 0.72x NAV and an 18% yield the stock already discounts weak coverage.
findings.independence: Miss history from the MarketBeat preview (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-saratoga-investment-sar-set-to-announce-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-09-29/) and the investing.com Q1 transcript summary (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-saratoga-investment-misses-q1-2026-estimates-as-stock-falls-93CH-4782007). The run-rate itself is my inference from the 10-Q, not a document number.

findings.finding: The 2026-09-22 prospectus supplement shows SBA debentures at $259.0m on Sep 21 against $213m at May 31, which uses the whole $46m of undrawn SBA capacity. The Valley SPV facility went from $32.5m to $47.5m. Total debt rose ~$53m even after the 6.00% notes were redeemed. SBA debentures can only fund qualifying SBIC investments, so this documents net deployment of roughly $50m+ across June to September, on top of Q1's $31m net originations.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Saratoga leads every release with AUM growth; Q1's +1.6% AUM headline did not offset the NAV and NII miss (-14.09%). Asset growth has not carried a print on its own in the baseline's seven reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: The debt-as-of-Sep-21 table sits in a note prospectus that equity aggregators do not read. If the deployment had been priced, the stock would not have fallen ~12% since the July print to a new low while the sector narrative focused only on refinancing costs.
findings.independence: The Q1 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001377936/000121390026075941/ea029727501ex99-1.htm) gives the May 31 starting point of $46m undrawn SBA and $196.8m total capacity, and the call cited a 'robust' pipeline. Same issuer, different document. Financing question answered: the money funds deployment, so the sign is positive.

findings.finding: The $105.5m of 6.00% 2027 notes were redeemed 2026-09-18 with $117.8m of 8.00% 2031 notes, and $20m of Valley debt at SOFR+2.85% is being termed out at 8%. That adds about $0.6m a quarter (~$0.035/share) of interest expense from Q3. The Sept 16 Fed hike to 3.75-4.00% adds about $0.45m a quarter after incentive fee on mostly floating assets against mostly fixed liabilities. Net forward NII is a small headwind, and the $75m of 4.35% notes due Feb 2027 still has to be refinanced near 8%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No guidance is given. Dividend-coverage commentary is the de facto guide, and its deterioration accompanied the -14.09% July reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the sector narrative ('bond issuance remains an income headwind') and the 18% yield already discount it. It is held at a token size because the call is where management first quantifies the net walk.
findings.independence: Fed decision (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/16/fed-rate-decision-september-2026.html). The rate-hike offset is macro-to-company inference, not a company statement.

outside_window.finding: The dividend reset risk is real (NII ~$0.47 against a $0.75 quarterly dividend, spillover ~$1.50/share falling ~$0.26 a quarter), but the Q3 dividend of $0.75 was already declared on 2026-09-09. The next declaration, where a cut would land, is expected around early December 2026.

baseline_tension: The small net negative agrees with the tape (52-week low, -9% over 20 days, 6 of 7 prior reactions negative), so most of it is already in the price; the one document-backed item, deployment, cuts the other way. There is no skew to beat.
lessons_applied: Rule 6: the $0.49 bar has one confirmed source (Benzinga's $0.54 is stale and disagrees), so every finding is capped small. F1 cut from -0.8 to -0.5 and print_vs_bar from -3.0 to -2.0.

Rule 5: F1's run-rate and F3's rate-hike offset are inference, not company numbers, which is a further reason they stay token-sized. F2 rests on a primary document (prospectus debt table) and stays at +0.4.

Rule 4: the refinancing and SBA/Valley draws were treated as a question. The answer is that the money funds deployment and maturity extension, not distress, so F2 is positive and F3 shrank from -0.3 to -0.2.
Rule 6: the dividend-cut risk is dated after the window (next declaration ~December), so it sits in outside_window, not in findings.
Rule 3: baseline_tension says the negative agrees with an already-depressed tape, so expected_move equals the reduced sum (-0.3) rather than leaning further on the 6-of-7 negative reaction history.
